label: De Rham Cohomology
notes: This chapter, printed pages 440 through 466, turns the failure of closed forms to be exact into a sequence of computable invariants. We open with the guiding question: when can we solve d eta equals omega globally, and what obstruction stops us when the manifold has a hole.

label: The de Rham Complex
notes: Everything rests on d squared equals zero, which guarantees images sit inside kernels. I want students to see the cochain complex as a chain of vector spaces and maps, with closed forms as kernels and exact forms as images stacked one stage earlier in the sequence.

label: Cohomology Groups
notes: Here we define the p-th de Rham cohomology as closed modulo exact. Stress that this is a quotient vector space, that its elements are equivalence classes of closed forms differing by exact forms, and that a nonzero class is a genuine global obstruction to integration.

label: H-zero Counts Components
notes: The degree zero group is the friendliest case. A closed zero-form is a locally constant function, exactness is empty in degree zero, so the dimension of H-zero equals the number of connected components. This grounds cohomology in something students already picture clearly.

label: The Angle Form
notes: This is the chapter's signature example. The angle form on the punctured plane is closed everywhere yet has loop integral two pi around the origin, so it cannot be globally exact. Walk the room through why local antiderivatives exist but cannot be glued consistently.

label: Induced Maps and Functoriality
notes: Because pullback commutes with the exterior derivative, a smooth map descends to a linear map on cohomology. Emphasize the functor laws: identity goes to identity and composition reverses order, so diffeomorphic manifolds automatically have isomorphic cohomology.

label: Homotopy Invariance
notes: The deep theorem: homotopic maps induce equal cohomology maps. The engine is the homotopy operator h satisfying d h plus h d equals the difference of the two endpoint pullbacks. I show the cylinder picture so students see integration along the interval direction producing an exact term.

label: The Poincare Lemma
notes: Homotopy invariance pays off immediately. A contractible or star-shaped region is homotopy equivalent to a point, so all higher cohomology vanishes. Every closed p-form on such a region is exact. This is the local triviality that makes cohomology a purely global measurement.

label: Computing the Circle
notes: Now we compute. The circle has H-zero and H-one both equal to R; the angle form generates the one-dimensional first cohomology. Connect this back to the punctured plane, which deformation retracts to the circle and therefore shares its cohomology exactly.

label: Mayer-Vietoris
notes: This is the main computational machine. An open cover by U and V produces a long exact sequence linking the cohomology of the union, the pieces, and the intersection. The connecting homomorphism is where new global classes are born from mismatches on overlaps.

label: Mayer-Vietoris on the Circle
notes: I run the circle through Mayer-Vietoris concretely. Two contractible arcs whose intersection has two components force a one-dimensional cokernel, and the connecting map produces exactly the generator of H-one. This rank bookkeeping is the heart of the notebook computation.

label: Spheres and Top Degree
notes: The sphere computation falls out by induction with Mayer-Vietoris: the n-sphere has R in degrees zero and n and zero between. Top-degree cohomology of a compact connected oriented manifold is R, detected by integrating an orientation form over the whole space.

label: Degree of a Map
notes: The payoff is degree theory. A smooth map between compact oriented manifolds of equal dimension carries an integer degree, computable either by comparing integrals of a pulled-back top form or by counting signed preimages of a regular value. For the circle map z to z to the k, both give k.

label: Recap
notes: We close by tying the thread together. Cohomology measures the obstruction to global exactness, the Poincare lemma kills it locally, homotopy invariance makes it topological, and Mayer-Vietoris computes it. Holes become numbers, and those numbers feed degree theory and the rest of differential topology.
